title: The week the Fed's next move started pointing upwards
dek: A hot October CPI print put a December rate rise on the table in Washington, Frankfurt and Tokyo — and shares rallied anyway.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.explanation: The VIX fell about a quarter over the week to 19.3 and high-yield credit spreads tightened to 3.2 percentage points, which is not what a frightened market looks like. Yet CNN's Fear & Greed index is still at 39, in 'fear', and Reddit chatter remains fixated on a handful of chip names rather than broad index funds.

regions.headline: Hot CPI turns the Fed debate from cuts to hikes
regions.summary: October consumer prices rose 0.4% on the month, taking annual CPI to 4.08%, and officials began openly discussing a December increase — even half a point. Two-year yields hit 4.86% and the 10-year closed at 5.15%. Shares still rose 2.5% on the week. The 30-year mortgage averaged 7.11% on 12 November, so borrowing costs are not easing.

regions.headline: Growth holds up, and so does the ECB's inflation worry
regions.summary: Euro-area GDP grew 1.28% in the year to the third quarter, with inflation at 3.75% in September and the deposit rate at 2.50%. A Reuters poll of economists now expects 2.75% in December. In Britain, the Bank's chief economist flagged further rises; Moody's cut its French growth forecast for 2026 to 0.2%.

regions.headline: Yen near 160 as Tokyo and Delhi face rate pressure
regions.summary: The yen slid to almost 160 per dollar as the Bank of Japan's October summary showed members debating faster rate rises. The Nikkei still gained 6.5% on the week. India's October inflation hit a two-year high of 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% ceiling, with food prices up 8.94% — a direct squeeze on household budgets.

body:
For most of this year the argument was about how fast central banks would cut. This week it flipped. A hotter-than-expected October inflation report in the United States had Fed officials talking about raising rates in December, economists polled by Reuters expect the ECB to do the same, and the Bank of Japan is being nudged in the same direction by a yen near 160. Three threads run through it all: inflation that will not finish the job, an oil market caught between tanker attacks and a glut, and an AI complex rattled by the abrupt exit of its most famous chief executive.

## United States

The number that moved everything was small. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than forecast, with food and rent doing the damage, and [core prices rose 0.3%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxPdHFNQ2h0OXJRbGQxN2dWLVp5bV96cVdoejZvN0U4WmlWVmw5dTZYbWtraGpleXA1REZtaERNRDE5ODg4TFpQQk0xZjd2bWR6WHptbDBSM3UwbWJxbGVNdm9SbFVoUVFXVFlnQ3V4TFk5RXBLS24yUHExT2FBc2FjM0xYclpZUFZhUFJNTURKUkNPUV90QXJHQkhNLTROd05DNHJsMmttWjVlb1JVZU9zWGdYTQ?oc=5). That took annual CPI to 4.08%, up from 4.02% in September, with core at 2.87%. It was the [third brisk month in a row](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxQLWo2UHlxSDlLcGNITjBhSkhrVmNFMDZNZ29xNEdoZ045dWRUV3JoQXQ1MUZCRlNlbHBqMnh2cG1iWjN1STQzNy1OWTZSLXZONmdLZHp1V29LbWxUcnVQS0JwNFVtR3dmOXlDRVcxLXdHWldWek03TXRvU2x5aTgyR1hhVTIyb3R5NUVvdl93aEhHempGNUFtVFVfTQ?oc=5), and it broke the story the market had been telling itself.

Fed officials reacted quickly. Several [opened the door to a half-point move](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiwwFBVV95cUxOTXo5UzFWVEh5WllQOHNxS1Q2cERxOEM0X1QyN1dPX0R4XzdfT1BpajYxdi0xOEltNWh6cE15Z2ZvZ2dXV0Vwb3NkbWZ1VGQ2M2tvVVVSaWd6clhPcS1XUEU2QXE3c0tlLUhPX0c2emRnWVpwOGtoajlnSS1VRXRNZXFaNEpyVlVwcFVIOUdkT18yQ2t6a1psZGVlOFpiZl90QnVhcmxqQzNxNnlNSEdXcWpjcUdzYUNJSi1hcnl6ZEpUSUU?oc=5), and by Friday Bloomberg had the Fed [on track to raise rates next month and possibly again in January](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMivAFBVV95cUxNeXJmalVqcjF1WEgxXzRyZ2hNRTRMWXdCWGdpblhnaGwxY0ZDeFIwYTVnWENtQ2U2NFg3YkpUS21EdkNHaXlwVlVicGxWd2RJZnJqOXlySXJfZzdscXlqRFNJSkswUjZ0ZjFINC11aU9GMWdrMGR6SzdfYUlkN3pGaDZZci1NbnkxWmtoZ1lNa3E2MmxDcnFqRnN0MWpwUURLT05odHBpdVlhNXRjNUJOd3JGcnNCYzd6bjVqWQ?oc=5). That is a remarkable turn for a committee whose policy rate averaged 3.88% in October. The Treasury, meanwhile, [warned against tightening into an energy shock](https://news.google.?oc=5) caused by the conflict with Iran — a rare public split over who should absorb a supply-driven price rise.

Bond markets did the arithmetic. The two-year yield reached 4.86% on 12 November and the 10-year closed the week at 5.15%, roughly 0.29 percentage points higher than a week earlier. The 30-year mortgage averaged 7.11% in the week to 12 November, barely changed. In plain terms: if you are refinancing a loan or fixing a mortgage, the starting point just got more expensive, and the gap between two- and ten-year yields of 0.27 points says the market expects rates to stay high rather than spike and fall. Shares shrugged, with the S&P 500 up 2.5% on the week.

## Euro area

Europe is having a gentler version of the same conversation. Growth held up — the euro area expanded 1.28% in the year to the third quarter, slightly better than the 1.19% of the previous quarter — and [the ECB is weighing another rise](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxOYVZieW1jVWE1WGMzSlU1a2w5czJmbHJWaEMybDd3OUpRQUxELWJVbE1IcGVUcjF1eXMwNDVBUGduSk1MTVpnWWhuNFo4U0c5R3FWTVh0UFFtQVpTRmgyd1NpWC14bTBwTVM5Z01WSC1oWFJ2aWpYaXAxOUlrRUdVVk05dEo0UEZaeG82Zlg1UzBXazZjTmRLQ093a2x6eV96S3dET1NBeTY2RkZtV3FDSw?oc=5) with inflation at 3.75% in September. [Economists polled by Reuters now expect 2.75% in December](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxQcWlZMUVPZXI0OS0zbnpNSUFLWl9UajYyRkJpN1JBQ0tDVEQtcDhxS21TelZ2UkQzV2I1bWZ4ZGJnN1NtdmhVNm00djNLTG4yYnlNQXVWbmZIbDQzSFJiS250enBTdXJZZ3FqeFdiU0dWYm95U2NWWTZyODBkeTM5akloMDdhZmZkVDB2VVVJRHJIbERkSGlFZXcyNFo1WnJTYWRTTkFGWDFwOGhNb3IwR1M5UnFFN3Na?oc=5), up from the current 2.50% deposit rate, after the Bundesbank chief flagged inflation risks. Lagarde has said inflation will stay high but that [second-round effects are not worse than anticipated](https://news.google.?oc=5) — central-bank language for wage demands not yet spiralling.

Not every economy is pulling the same weight. Moody's cut its forecast for French growth this year [to 0.2%](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMitwFBVV95cUxOZ0JZYmF3b053Q1ZHcXBVN0RULV90WlhkN25yNDhWd25ZYkdkU0F3VzBhZEFfcFRSaWxJdHA0VkZlQVlZRU9YMGsyd1JXeUVVZDNTRm5VZ0paR2h4X05XT1ZXYVZlQXo0ckxDVFFRUTR5T2dMbVA5YmVWZVBucV9nREhJRHJxMUlaUEhlZnJuT1R1UXl4NzRUUkZaQUNzTE55X1NWQ0FQck1PZkV5VFM0T0FFeUxHbWM?oc=5), and French protests against austerity continue, which matters because France was already paying 4.48% on ten-year borrowing in September against Germany's 3.47%. In Britain, the Bank of England's chief economist said [further rate rises are likely in the coming months](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxNbTJTaDRiMXdzRmJWYTFnR2RDak1FNklXdm5sT0pYQUlXZzFtZkVVT3VER1g3dEpKb0YzSzRiS0JBWE1RbFJ1czJ0MnZSOE1QZGt0TF9sRUNrSGJ3YmZpVDFvMlVpdmhvMVdIbHhQcnZpVFdleTVmb1lCRzRNcm9CejIxdVZPVF9NNjR4ZDJ0Q01ZVGxoNnQyYkEyU1J5T0FGSUlueGJxeUdtVlJaaDJB?oc=5), while a Reuters poll leans towards February. The Treasury also [opened an investigation into a leak of Budget bank-tax plans](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMijwFBVV95cUxOdlR5ekVMQl9nRXR0TG8wa0QtanA4Ni1sMlpXOEtPcHpUSml3UTg0dWFqVWRGSGU2VXg4dWhGOWI2cU9lVDluRGU4cDFuajhheVl5MFZILWFscWpBOHFQN0d5UmdIbTcyY3p2QnJkV1FMZi1MWlJGOFRvZEFfV3M4b2YwcnJtazI2RU1MNTNfOA?oc=5). European shares did well regardless: the DAX gained 3.6% on the week, the Euro Stoxx 50 3.5%.

## Asia

The yen is the pressure gauge. It [slid towards 160 per dollar](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMipAFBVV95cUxQM3EzbUZLMzVNX1JTTVVjTVYwOVhoR0JQMXlRWjh3WjA3OGlfRkhvek43Qk90UW1jeWVDOWZMa2djT0JlSnhoRUh3SXBtbWpRQ1Q5SkNJbnVhZHR5X2NsWTFLT0w4TG4tOEdXQlBVdG91RGp1aWFtNkxJN3NZYktEN1dRWWU3LWQ3MTJ3SjNKejBkc1Zsb3JTV3Myd2t5SnZEeHRaZQ?oc=5) as traders priced in US rate rises, even though the Bank of Japan's own October summary showed members [debating whether to go faster](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirwFBVV95cUxPVlFiYV9MUkZPd3FBcDV4X3lEQkJjNWlRTHUzU3ZKTDZYcGhYelZlSDB6aEhtckNFa2stVGE3SFhrRzQwU1JfTGNPSmM4Tmt3VkpIbDRpUFc5QlpScFRReFVNX2tKUDRIRUVtTHpoMmdRekI4d1VmclIyTXMzSkFfdXU0dVhidG1lVHdBTllMaVhJMkdnWGROcEVjNk11SGZLOVNHcnNmUDIwbG5PMWVJ?oc=5). A weak yen flatters Japanese exporters — the Nikkei jumped 6.5% in the week to 61,142 — but it makes every imported barrel and every food shipment dearer for Japanese households, which is precisely why Tokyo is being pushed to move.

India had the week's most uncomfortable print. October inflation rose to 6.09%, a two-year high that [breached the Reserve Bank's 6% upper limit](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNSlE4RjR5cTc2cVI3bWZZWHJxcGdTTXA4UjBQNUEtbVdfeXJwdXZ1b21ZejRTaERGWmlXa0JDZ2ZKWHdBaUx3cVFwRnlTSzVzci1FakptNjVUWVZZYXZ2WEEwVy1LMktOWFlUdE5GNHpLbTBMNTR2VFFwRHUtSDFqUkNnUkFNUDBBR2Z0Zm84YjZraTJnaV9uUEU1NVZGN0xnaHVIMWVxRFNiOEsyelNQdWI0R1Y3UVpZ?oc=5), with food inflation at 8.94%. When food is nearly 9% dearer than a year ago, rate decisions stop being abstract. Elsewhere the picture split: the Sensex rose 2.9% and the KOSPI 4.6%, while the Hang Seng fell 3.5% and Shanghai slipped slightly. China's October activity data lands next week, and the APEC gathering in Shenzhen is [the city's toughest logistical test yet](https://news.google.?oc=5).

## Debt and politics

Politics is now a rates story. Democrats took Congress in the midterms, and Trump [heads to Asia hoping to shift momentum](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilgFBVV95cUxPU1NqQ012SUxkSlBybGhjS290cUFLdzVaU0NabWlVbkN3Y3IzbzRqTGsteHlBOFMwUFF6M21sa0lhVGZsaUM2MkZwaHBCN3ZqRGVKSk5DWFdOVGhVR2JHcXo2OXFtQTNrUm9jSWxqWVZ0cndRMHB0UnRtWm1rc29heE9xLXdtRnhhZ0tCdW1yZHlhVEJTN0E?oc=5), with a [meeting alongside Xi and Putin](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikgFBVV95cUxPeHprMDZOSFVJbjlUVk9oYVl0czEzcHk0eHFpR3NBUGhRMWpDU1BvdTlQLVFTdE9EOXdYRVpWT1hfVzg4dkljS2NLYmVOUm9vcWs0QVRiRTVQdkttOFZXT0xPUFZwazJmQzhVWEpzZzdrX2kydUF4T2owbDIyU0trMnlmV1EzbXJJY21HSWdKS3Vhdw?oc=5) announced by the White House. On Ukraine, Zelenskyy says Washington [floated exchanging territory for NATO membership](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMicEFVX3lxTE04V3RucGdlaGp6dm03UnM5TmRsMTQyVTBSZ1JxOHc3ZGJDeFRMOUFMUWlFR21wR05kaXJqcENqZG5URXJrMVN4MnMxVUU4UDhYNW05X2FVbHdyVzVZa3pSZk1NZFFObk0tZThid1RSX2g?oc=5), while Estonia prepares to [close its border with Russia](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxNX2hUV0NzQ2diVFk2akVsWHJLa2dGenpKNHBjQkR6QS13eV9UNENTTWsySWR2WmZDNFlfSXJQZE10cjBSX1VVUXAtM2pVcnJUTDVVMGZVbjRnNTR2N3JaNGtNaTZGNDBHT0pqaDVjcFV0RnhJUmFhV250TG9sUGw2enhxdUpEQWpLX2hwTXNUcDdTOWFwcEZzR2NjcnJBTWdObjBFTlZXeUlvMXhCSEE?oc=5) after sabotage attacks. None of this is priced in any tidy way, but it shapes energy and defence spending, and therefore inflation.

The fiscal backdrop is unchanged and unforgiving. US federal debt stood at 121.2% of GDP in the second quarter and the deficit was 5.75% of GDP in the 2025 fiscal year; euro-area government debt edged up to 88.8%. Here is the catch: if the Fed raises rather than cuts, every government refinancing maturing paper pays more, and the Eurogroup's call for [fiscal discipline alongside joint defence spending](https://news.google.?oc=5) gets harder to honour.

## AI and technology

The AI trade lost its figurehead. Jensen Huang [resigned as Nvidia's chief executive](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMikwFBVV95cUxON2VaZ01EcWdXc1ZGb3plNUNMM294WGZlT0tTbWw2SFNPOHZ3ZERtQlR6RkhLRWF2cHExRnNfWGZINm1NWVoxVjRSUDRTVXRFb1RaRGcyMXFUdEd0LWtlME5SVHJETVdzOHR6eHhyNXJLVXF6cldFbnhHMXcydFMzTGhzVnhWN2RQX2d0X1N4QVZvdUU?oc=5) amid an alleged espionage scandal, Treasury Secretary Bessent said the company needs a [dramatic shake-up](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisgFBVV95cUxNS1ZOWlF3ZUlxWGYyZm9kX3NnZUsyNEpjYXhKaWMxY3hPbnRvSlJYeHc3ak9lejRYcHdmWjB2dk54cmMweklHdXdpVDdmRm9yNE91LWJKV2VoUC16bF9sdzRTM2NhWk5MMnBROXJ2UHA2SU0tSDNpeEZLZkxJZGg4T1laVHUyU1Fid0dtYjQ3c0tHMFRsOVp3TndoeEUzaElUSkxVT3hlOGQyZTVPZDF3emxB?oc=5), and Congress is [moving to tighten AI chip export rules](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMihAFBVV95cUxQVGxvZmxUQ0JxLVJuWmRILTBpbUwwbEMxbDV1bEhkYVdjdnl3WVYzWFBGZFhqckFER1JyYWptWEI3XzAzeEZ1dnZuSUdYVkFCdFZXTjVmMUxtVjJSc0dPZHR2R05TbE1mQzA0OU84TEdXd1I0UkFrS2Z0dDRIUXoxV2Y3b2o?oc=5) in response. Into that lands Anthropic's flotation: a price range of [$70 to $78 with trading due to start on 19 November](https://news.google.?oc=5), targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion, and reportedly [six times oversubscribed](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxQeWxnOC1MRXVQbUJwaDdiSDE3TzdIbVRyYU5qWnF5YzkycUVPTXV0bUhOWEIzWU1xejMyQXJxaGtHT2dQbk1iTExkc29hYjBpQWRsY3RTaEtsTVhVaFJjOHl5aW5nb0dDYzRwcWxjVXpkbWw1bU5lSFhwVHo4aGw4bHJZYlNZTUVoN2VwYnhBWmNDNURMbXNmN2FvaEVONS1CVG1MY004MzdMbTRJd1E2eQ?oc=5). Add a [widespread Microsoft outage](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMifkFVX3lxTE9SZmZCcS1rWDBlU1EtNTRYbFY4TE00cEVObWk3ak9jcnNsaWtabW83MjNuemxSUk1WWXZ5Q2VubUtCZ2Y5YnZkN2dNR3htVEhHUkpPbjNuczc0VmpDb1dIZ0Z3TVFaTW43Z1hrc00tTWFQQ0M5cFd4SUd6TG1ldw?oc=5) and an FAA ground stop, and it was a week that tested faith in the machines.

## Company news and results

One quarterly filing captured the cost environment better than any survey. Lithium Americas told the SEC on 12 November that its definitive capital cost estimate for Phase 1 of the Thacker Pass project in Nevada is now $3.83 billion, up from $2.93 billion previously. The company attributed roughly $100 million to tariffs and logistics — citing higher fuel prices and rerouted shipping — about $150 million to craft wage escalation, and about $245 million to installation labour rates, as [reported in its own release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1966983/000119312526456875/lac-ex99_1.htm). Those are the three inflation channels economists keep describing, itemised in dollars by one builder.

Elsewhere, Italy fined Meta $887m over [access to Android users' photos and videos](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxOTW9mbXFBUUVjX2R6d19QWTBrWlFiSE96OFVjeGx1elljZGJnYkdLbnhlRy11d1BObUpPN0Vvam40bTBieFJwdGNhY0NrWE5iMG1FT3E3SnFQU0FiMm13ZmZzX0xYQXA5aG1od3FHanp1U2pWVnY1eTZ3VFR0WmYyc0VVNFVXVGIwdkFJVWdwNl85dEpIS1dFWmR4NXNfOU1tc2pZRlFtTElMV25lMU9hYWV0Njh3RUtuaGc?oc=5), and the FDA rejected Summit's ivonescimab, [halting the US arrival of that drug class](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMimwFBVV95cUxPRUFJWnNTQ00yaXJYT21NN1BCMUdpM3BjbjdyUk9WOEFIcGx4U090RlVIbXp6OGVjTkFBREhGUnUtclFRU3d5OS1PVkVNQk9tZGVGSS1wZmNMamlleFBMalZUQzFrNXB5TGN5SzFMd3REcTZCcG5IQXpMMkFYc2lac0VEbnZ4V2NuSTZ4VVJrRnd6TkJfdUtJWmt6VQ?oc=5).

## Market mood

The tape and the sentiment surveys disagree. The VIX, which measures expected swings in US shares, fell about a quarter over the week to 19.3, and high-yield credit spreads — the extra interest riskier companies pay to borrow — narrowed to 3.2 percentage points on 12 November. That is a market functioning calmly. Yet CNN's Fear & Greed index sits at 39, still "fear", even after climbing from 24 a week earlier, gold fell 4.6% and bitcoin dropped 12% to about $64,800 amid a [slow-motion crypto selloff](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiswFBVV95cUxQbkNtd29JSVN3NktDZF9RamdWQlQySzg4UzBEUFZkeWkxY2JINnFlZEFyMHd1c1FoSEsxcjZEN3F5V2R4WlZ6djdQQllXNDNqVWo1SnZWTlNpY3Ywb2w3QVNuTlI3UzdtUFg2RWFUYnktM3VRWFJUSWY0a1BIYUdxc19HVnk2ZGZxY2t3UXdEeGpqY0lhclFZVXhFN01vUXFxcFZ5b2E5WmxYX1lXSnJWMnprTQ?oc=5). Reddit chatter stayed concentrated on a few chip names rather than broad index funds — attention, not conviction.

## What to watch next week

Two dates carry most of the weight. The minutes of the last Fed meeting will show how seriously officials were already discussing a rise before the October CPI print landed, which is the difference between a December move being a surprise and a formality. Then US retail sales tell you whether households are still spending through 4% inflation. Japan's third-quarter GDP and China's October activity data fill in the other half of the world.
